svg.data-input: AC 100 to 240V, 2A max x2; DC -36 to -75V, 4.5A max x2
svg.data-cooling: fanless; the rack must supply at least 1 m/s of airflow in any direction without recirculation (HIG Cooling), and 43.5 mm of clear space is required above and below the unit when the ambient is between 45 and 65 C
svg.data-optics-sfp: 1G SFP SX/LX/EX/ZX, up to 70 km (datasheet Compatible Transceivers; HIG Port Overview gives 100M/1G on ports 0-7)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER/ZR, up to 80 km (datasheet Compatible Transceivers; HIG Port Overview gives 1/10G on ports 8-11)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2, T-BC/OC, T-TC) - NOS integration required to activate, and SMPTE ST 2059-2 needs an additional licence (the vendor's own footnotes)
svg.data-timing-inputs: 1x 1PPS in/out SMB, 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, 1x ToD in/out RJ45
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55035; EN 300 386; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A; SANS 2332 Class A; SANS 2335; BSMI

HIG Figure 5's callout names it 'Reset' and no other button exists on this panel."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - 'Chassis (WxDxH) 1 RU, 440 x 250 x 43.5mm or 17.32' x 9.84' x 1.713\" Weight: 4.26kg or 9.39lb'; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the dimensions ('S9502-12SM (W x D x H) 17.32' x 9.84' x 1.71' (440 x 250 x 43.5mm)') and the weight ('Chassis without FRU 9.39lbs (4.26kg)'). 440 is the body between the ear folds, not a rack face: the HIG Space Clearance section separates 'The S9502-12SM width is 17.32 inches (44cm)' from the 'rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and the brackets ship loose (50.4 x 43 x 20 mm accessories, 8 M4 screws) and can go at the front or the centre of the side, so there is no ear extent to subtract. DEPTH IS THE ONE TO READ TWICE: 250 is the body, and HIG Figure 5's top view dimensions BOTH it and D = 10.39\" (264 mm) over the front connectors, the 14 mm difference being the projection the Space Clearance section states as 0.55 inches. chassis.depth carries the body; the 14 mm lives on the connector parts' relief."},"fanless":{"note":"the defining fact about this box and the reason it has no fan bays at all. The datasheet key feature is 'Fanless chassis design', the HIG's Cooling paragraph is 'The S9502-12SM has a fanless design so the rack or cabinet must have a minimum of 3.28 feet/second (1 meter/second) airflow in any direction without recirculation', and its Preparation Check List gives the airflow direction as 'front-to-back and back-to-front' - i.e. convection either way, which is why no configuration here declares an airflow. Figure 5's fourth strip is captioned 'Fanless' and points at the rear's six vent patches. The heat leaves through those, through the front vent fields and through the side vents; all three are drawn."},"front-layout":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - the vendor front render s9502-12sm-2-front.png. GATE 1: the render IS the chassis edge to edge, 1717 x 170 px, aspect 10.10 against the datasheet's 10.115 (440/43.5) - 0.15% out, the closest any source in this intake has come, at 3.902 px/mm. Every front number below is measured on it, and HIG Figures 5, 6 and 8 corroborate the arrangement. Left to right: two fixed-PSU input windows, the two SMB timing jacks under the model name, the four system lamps and the RESET button, the OOB/USB bezel plate, the ToD/console bezel plate, a hex vent field, the eight SFP cages, the four SFP+ cages, more vent field, and the earth symbol marking the side-mounted grounding lug."},"left-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - the two bezel plates and their contents, all off the front render. The OOB/USB plate is silver x 165.54-181.69, y 13.84-34.60, split by an internal rail into the OOB RJ45 aperture (y 15.38-23.83) and the USB-A aperture (y 28.19-33.31). The ToD/console plate is silver x 187.07-202.96, y 9.48-34.85, split into two equal RJ45 apertures (y 11.28-20.50 and 24.09-33.31). Both RJ45 pairs are drawn with std/rj45-ganged because each plate is one piece of metal about 16 mm wide and a 16 mm single-port IEC bezel does not fit two of them in it. The OOB jack's two integrated lamps are visible in the render (green left, amber right) and now draw as led-a/led-b of the jack."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9502-12SM end of life' - no announcement found. The vendor lists the product on its telecom solutions pages and it remains a current cell-site gateway. none-announced is a checked state, not an absence."},"port-grid":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - and the lamps are the ruler again. The eight green \u25b2\u25bc lamp pairs give column centres 311.79 / 326.05 / 340.18 / 354.56 for the SFP block and 372.94 / 387.28 for the SFP+ block: a pitch of 14.257 and 14.34 against SFF-8433's 14.25 Basic, which is as close as a 3.9 px/mm image can come to the standard. Ports are placed at each column centre minus half of std/sfp-ganged's 14.25, so the SFP block runs x 304.67 / 318.92 / 333.18 / 347.44 and the SFP+ block 365.82 / 380.07. The SFP+ block's blue paint independently measures x 365.43-394.90, which brackets those two columns to within 0.4 mm at each end."},"port-numbering":{"note":"HIG Port Overview table: 'Port ID 0~7 SFP 100M/1G, 8~11 SFP+ 1/10G'. The panel prints the numerals large above and below each column - 0 2 4 6 over 1 3 5 7 on the SFP block, 8 10 over 9 11 on the SFP+ block - so even ports are the top row and odd the bottom, read directly off the front render. The SFP+ numerals sit on the blue paint strips and are white; the SFP ones sit on bare panel."},"port-rows":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - the cages are two rows belly-to-belly, and the silver band between them measures y 19.22-25.11 in the SFP block and 18.71-25.11 in the SFP+ block. Setting std/sfp-ganged's 10.4 mm opening against those edges puts the top row at y 8.6 and the bottom at 25.1, a row pitch of 16.5 against the component's own measured belly-to-belly 15.0 - the 1.5 mm is recorded rather than forced, because the band is what the image resolves and the 15.0 is a different device's caliper. The top row is rotate 180 so its latch faces the centre band, as the render draws both rows."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet gives 'Typical power: 45.1 Watts (no transceiver)'. The HIG's two Connecting Power sections give the maxima: 'The maximum system power consumption is 45 watts' (DC Version) and 'The maximum system power consumption is 47.2 watts with an input voltage of 100-240V AC and 2 amperes' (AC Version). NOTE WHAT THAT MEANS AND DO NOT SMOOTH IT: the DC maximum, 45 W, is LOWER than the datasheet's typical, 45.1 W. Both are the vendor's, from two documents, and they are not reconciled here - power-max-w carries the AC 47.2, power-max-dc-w the 45, and power-typical-w the 45.1, with this sentence as the record that the last two cross. Neither source states a test condition for these figures - no ambient, no optics population, no traffic load, unlike every other UfiSpace box in this library - so power-envelope is `unstated` rather than a guess at `fully-configured`."},"psu-inputs":{"note":"THE SUPPLIES ARE FIXED AND THE BAYS DO NOT MEAN OTHERWISE. The datasheet's Redundancy row is 'Fixed, 1+1 redundant PSU' and the HIG's section 4 headings are 'DC Version PSU Overview - 1+1, Fixed power supply unit (PSU)' and the same for AC. What the front panel carries is each supply's input connector, not a removable module, so it is drawn as a PLACEMENT and not a bay - nothing here should imply it pulls out. Only the DC build is drawn: see gaps for why the AC build turned out to be a different panel rather than a swapped connector. Geometry: the DC terminal blocks measure x 19.5-52.8 and 75.6-108.9 (a 56.13 step read from the screw centres 22.29 and 78.42), y 18.1-34.0; the AC C14 apertures measure x 21.34-48.12, y 15.35-34.08 on HIG Figure 5's AC elevation. The shared bay is sized 33.3 x 21.0 to hold both. The printed legends 'RTN -36 \u2014 -75 \u2393 \u23da' and 'RNT -36 \u2014 -75 \u2393 \u23da' are transcribed as printed: the second reads RNT in the front render AND in HIG Figure 6, which is a vendor typo for RTN reproduced in two independent places, and tidying it would be inventing artwork the device does not have."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - the vendor rear render s9502-12sm-4-rear.png (1648 x 165 px, aspect 9.988 against a true 10.115, 1.3% out, 3.745 px/mm - usable but the softest source here). Six circular hex vent patches on an even 49.93 mm pitch, x 25.9-64.1, 75.8-114.0, 125.8-164.2, 175.7-214.1, 225.9-264.1 and 275.8-314.0, each about 38 across and spanning y 5.1-39.0; the right-hand 125 mm of the panel is blank. This is the face HIG Figure 5 captions 'Fanless'. Five screw heads are visible along the bottom edge and are placed by eye at about 18.7 / 118.8 / 217.6 / 317.7 / 416.4, y 37.3 - ESTIMATED, because they are dark on a dark panel and no threshold separates them at 3.7 px/mm."},"sides":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG Figure 15 is a genuine side elevation of this chassis, and a good one: the body in it measures 866 x 153 px for a 250 x 43.5 object, aspect 5.66 against a true 5.747, 1.5% out, at 3.464 px/mm. It shows the RIGHT side (the front is at its left, and the grounding pad it highlights is the one the front panel's earth symbol marks at x 434.8, the right-hand end). Measured on it: the grounding pad's two M4 holes at (8.6, 22.05) and (24.4, 22.05); the front bracket screw holes at (42.5, 9.4) and (42.5, 34.6); the centre bracket holes at (128.4, 9.3), (153.6, 9.3), (128.4, 34.6) and (153.6, 34.6) - a 25.1 x 25.3 rectangle, i.e. the 1-inch pattern the HIG's two bracket positions need; and two lower bracket screws at (116.3, 35.4) and (225.5, 35.4). Side vent fields run x 47-120 and x 165-245, y 6-38. AXIS CONVENTION: on the RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, so Figure 15 maps onto it unchanged; on the LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR (renderer convention), so the left view carries the same pattern mirrored as depth - x - width. The pattern is strongly asymmetric front-to-rear, so a wrong mirror would be visible here - which is why the convention is written beside the numbers. The grounding pad is drawn on the RIGHT side only; see gaps for what the HIG says about a second location."},"system-leds":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - four lamps in a vertical column at x 136.18, y 22.29 / 24.73 / 27.28 / 29.61, beside a printed white legend box at x 138.12-143.76, y 21.01-31.01. That is exactly the four the HIG front-panel LED table defines - SYNC, STAT, PSU, PWR - and the table's order matches the column top to bottom. The measured gaps are 2.44 / 2.55 / 2.33 and they are drawn on an even 2.44 pitch instead: one centreline for a lamp block, with the drawing's 0.11 mm scatter recorded here rather than copied. Drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, nearest part); states transcribed from the table."},"timing-jacks":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - the two SMB bezels are yellow rings centring (125.42, 8.37) and (125.44, 19.36), 6.4 x 6.7 across, each under its own printed legend (1PPS above the upper, 10MHZ above the lower). std/smb is the registry connector at 4.83 mm and is seated on those centres with the yellow bezel ring drawn as decor behind it, exactly as the S9321-64E does: the registry sizes the connector and the yellow is the washer around it. The third timing interface, ToD, is an RJ45 and is the upper jack of the right-hand bezel plate - the datasheet's 'Timing Interfaces (Standard)' row lists all three together and the HIG has a Connecting a Cable to the ToD Interface section for it."},"top":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG Figure 5's top view, which carries its own W = 17.32\" (440 mm) and D = 9.84\" (250 mm) dimension lines. GATE 1 IS MARGINAL: the drawn cover measures 2317 x 1389 px for a 440 x 250 object, aspect 1.668 against a true 1.760, 5.2% out, so no absolute scale is taken - the two groove positions below are fractions of the dimensioned 250. Two long recessed grooves, y 50.8-63.4 and 197.3-209.9 from the rear (centres 57.1 and 203.6, both 12.6 deep in the y axis). Their x extent is the weak number: the rims resolve top and bottom but not at the ends, so x 30-410 is ESTIMATED from the figure's proportions. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, the house convention, and this face carries nothing asymmetric front-to-back except the two grooves' own spacing, so the convention is stated rather than demonstrated."},"vents":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - three hex vent fields on the front: a strip over the PSU windows at x 19-106.5, y 1.0-8.5; a narrower strip along the top right at x 211.5-430.5, y 1.0-6.4; and the main field at x 243-431, y 10.7-32.0, which the two cage blocks are punched out of. rect.data-members: pps mhz mgmt usb tod console

g.data-description: the two FIXED 1+1 120W supplies. These do not pull out - what the front panel carries is each supply's input connector, drawn as a placement for that reason. Only the DC build is drawn; see gaps.
g.title: psu-0

g.data-description: the two FIXED 1+1 120W supplies. These do not pull out - what the front panel carries is each supply's input connector, drawn as a placement for that reason. Only the DC build is drawn; see gaps.
g.title: psu-1

g.data-description: 1PPS input/output, 50 ohm SMB with a 10-32UNF-2A connector; HIG Connecting the 1PPS Interface - cable no longer than 3 m
g.title: pps

g.data-description: 10MHz input/output, 50 ohm SMB; HIG Connecting the 10MHz Interface - cable no longer than 3 m
g.title: mhz

g.data-description: HIG SYNC row - Off (timing synchronization disabled or free-run), Solid Green (timing core, 1588 and SyncE, synchronized to an external source), Blinking Green (synchronized in SyncE mode), Solid Yellow (acquiring state or holdover), Blinking Yellow (synchronization fail). The table footnotes every row except holdover with 'need NOS to activate this feature'
g.title: led-sync

g.data-description: HIG STAT row - Off (system X86 and BMC initializing or not powered), Solid Green (system boot complete, NOS required to activate), Blinking Green (system is booting)
g.title: led-stat

g.data-description: HIG PSU row - Solid Green (both PSU feeds power good), Solid Yellow (PSU1 good, PSU2 not good), Blinking Yellow (PSU1 not good, PSU2 good), Off (the table says Reserved, so the dark state carries no meaning the vendor states)
g.title: led-psu

g.data-description: HIG PWR row - Off (system X86 and BMC initializing or not powered), Solid Green (system power good and CPU board power good), Blinking Green (system power fail, CPU board power good), Solid Yellow (system power good, CPU board power fail), Blinking Yellow (both fail)
g.title: led-pwr

g.data-description: the OOB management jack; its two integrated lamps (left green for 1G link and activity, right amber for 10M/100M, per the HIG Management port LED table) are drawn as led-a/led-b of this jack
g.title: mgmt

g.data-description: USB 2.0 Type-A; the HIG calls it a maintenance port
g.title: usb

g.data-description: ToD input/output, port marked TOD; HIG Connecting a Cable to the ToD Interface - a straight-through shielded Ethernet cable to a GNSS unit, no longer than 3 m
g.title: tod

g.data-description: the eight 100M/1G SFP ports, 0-7, in two belly-to-belly rows of four
g.title: port-0
